The game is viewed from behind the players at a elevated angle behind the court. The joystick moves the player and the fire button swings the racket. Pressing up and fire smashes a low ball and pressing down and fire lobs a high ball.

174087.overview: World Cup 90 is a soccer game capitalizing the event of World Cup of 1990 in Italy. All the national teams participating at the event are included; however, due to the lack of a license, the players' names are fictional. The player can create custom teams (name, tactics and color of the jersey) and change the team's roster. Multiplayer features two players mode (1 vs. 1 or 2 vs. CPU), and through additional interface, it is possible to add other two players.

174088.overview:
Based on the 1985 FIFA World Cup. The package included a Macmillan Books booklet and two programs, the "World Cup Fact File" and "World Cup Manager". 

The first program allowed you to see facts about the World Cup or participate with yourself or a friend in a quiz. The Facts section allowed you to see every result from every World Cup or how every team did as well. The Quiz section gave you 3 minutes to answer as many questions as you could from a choice of 5 answers. The quicker you answered a question the more points you received and if you played with a friend you took in it turns to answer a question. There was a high score table for the best scores.

The second program was a management game. Here you could choose any team that has played in the World Cup and attempt to get them to the final and win it. You are given a squad of players, or you can select your own. Choose your best team and it's onto the actual match. The 1st half lets you watch the match highlights in text form, with any major incidents appearing on the screen. Occasionally a penalty is awarded, and you can choose which direction to kick it or which direction your keeper should dive. An isometric view of the penalty is shown to see if it was missed or scored. In the 2nd half, you play two arcade sections to improve your score within a time limit. The two games are heading or shooting. The heading section is an isometric view, and the ball comes in from the side. You have to position your player to head the ball at the goal. The shooting section is shown from above and shows a football boot. A ball bounces around the screen, and you must move the boot to hit the ball into a moving net at the top of the screen. You must make sure the ball doesn't go past your boot into the net behind you. The computer decides how well you played and adds goals to your score or the oppositions.

174090.overview: World Geography is a quiz game that will help you learn many details about countries. This program covers 166 countries which are divided into 8 categories of difficulty. Each country is pinpointed on on accurate hi- resolution screen map of the world, and the user is asked the capital and/or population. At the end of the test, the percentage of correct answers is given, so that the student con monitor his geographical knowledge

174104.overview:
Time to take your favorite country from the bottom of the pile to be the best team in the world. Time to manage them and make them men, winning promotion from division 3 to division 1. After choosing your country you are taken to a list of options. Here you can pick your team, train them and check any injured players.

The actual match is shown in a TV studio with a presenter. Here you see a clock counting the minutes gone in the game. When there is a decisive moment the game switches to a overhead view of the pitch. Here you can see an attempt at a try or a kick at goal. Sometimes a try is scored or the player is tackled. If a try is scored then you watch the conversion attempt.

174105.overview:
Warner Thomas Fahrenheit is a stupid ball.
You have to help him and show the way to the goal (that blinking black box).

Use your joystick and scroll the screen. Warner tries to follow.

If you push the joystick longer Warner jumps higher.

Small push means smaller jumps. Warner's favourite place is the center of the screen.
Released in the 2018 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition and Reset Magazine prior to cartridge release.

174126.overview:
Our program transforms you into skilled pipe-fitter by adding one shaped piece at a time, whose shape is indicated in the square at the bottom left of the screen and which indicates the shape of the piece that you can insert in your scheme. Based on your initial optional choice on the type of game you intend to play, you can adjust what you have to do and where you have to place that particular piece. The goal is to display on the screen of your computer the starting point and the ending point of the pipeline to be built. The presentation screen brings up the cursor on the left side from which the piece indicated in the center of the square located at the bottom left. Move the cursor to where you want to lay pipe. The score will depend on the length of the pipeline built. 

Published in Italy as Worker Pipes in Videoteca Computer n.38.

174362.overview: A homebrew hockey management game from Chris R. Bickford III and released in 1989.

175733.overview: Webster: The Word Game is a word recognition game. The object of the game is to fill in the missing letters of an incomplete word. On each round a word will appear at the top of the screen with several letters missing. The word will slowly begin moving towards the bottom of the screen and along the bottom of the screen is the complete alphabet. The player needs to select the letters that are missing from the word before time runs out and the word reaches the bottom of the screen. Successfully completing a word earns points, but if the word reaches the bottom of the screen then the player loses a life. The game ends when all five lives are lost. There are several skill levels available which affect the time limit for each word and the complexity of the word. The game includes over 700 words of varying length and difficulty. Scoring in the game is based on how many correct/incorrect letters are selected and whether or not hints are utilized. In addition to the alphabet at the bottom of the screen are several asterisks; these represent hints. If more than one missing letter remains the player can choose a hint to fill in a missing letter in exchange for less points when the word is solved. On more difficult skill levels, a demon word will occasionally appear; demon words are more difficult and move very fast compared to the other words. If the player fails when a demon word appears a life is not lost, however hints are not available. Also, if a demon word is not solved then the solution will not be revealed to the player unlike normal words. On skill level 7 (the toughest) there are also challenge rounds which consist entirely of demon words; in this case failing a demon word does cost a life.

175763.overview: Education, education, education, that's the mantra. And one of the most important things to learn in American schools would be the names and capitals of all the US states. So here's something to help you do that.

175826.overview: Word Spinner is an educational game about pattern recognition and English language skills. The game features a "game show" feel to it, as the word spinner itself resembles a simple Wheel of Fortune and "prizes" are won during the course of the game. The goal is to form new words from the "clue" given. This clue can be blank spaces (e.g. form a three letter word) or include already assigned letters (e.g. form a three letter word, that starts with "t"). The goal is find 6 different words for each level, which will fill up the "word spinner", which represents a simple spinning wheel. Points are assigned for successful words, and every 300 points, the player is allowed to go to the prize spinner to select their winnings. Difficulty can be assigned between three and four letter words, and with different letters already embedded inside the word for the player to work with. Players are given the option of printing out the words they have found on the Word Spinner.

175969.overview: This Hungarian Joystick-only adventure will lead you on a merry chase. The theme is time travel and saving the earth. In the beginning you have to choose four items to take with you, that will be key to your success. The cracking group, Angels added unofficial English support in 2019.

175970.overview:
Welcome Aboard is an educational game that tries to help people become more computer literate with the help of the Muppets. There are 5 different activities included:

- The Bridge: help Kermit the Frog to steer the ship using a Logo-like programming language

- The Game Room: play an arcade style game under the protests of Sam the Eagle

- The Joke Library: learn fundamentals of database management by organizing Fozzie Bear's joke database

- The Message Center: learn how to use word processing and email with Scooter

- The Salon de Beaute: use a computer to find the perfect hairdo and outfit for Miss Piggy

175971.overview: Not to be confused with the Wheel of Fortune: NEW Third Edition is by a completely different publisher that came out several years before, this was an updated version by GameTek.

176012.overview:
Win, Lose or Draw Junior is the children's version for ages 8 - 15 of the popular game show. The game requires artistic skills and an ability to think laterally. A player on a team draws something on the big game board, and their other team member must work out what it represents. They will be common expressions depicted literally, such as 'bright idea' showing a light bulb over somebody's head, or 'cabin fever' as a rickety building next to a man with a thermometer in his mouth.

In this computerized implementation, the game is played as 3 teams, with one team drawing, while the other two teams try to correctly guess the answer. Categories are people, places, and things. If one of the two teams correctly guess the answer, the drawing and the correct guessing team both receive a point. The goal is to receive 3 points in all three categories, and that team is victorious. The drawing phase of the game is handled by the computer, so the player's task is simply to guess the meaning of the picture by thinking laterally. Each round allows 60 seconds to guess the answer, and if a player guesses incorrectly, they can not guess again until the other team has made an attempt.

176013.overview:
It's your own fault being trapped in this cellar. You ignored your wives warnings not to walk in the woods near your house as a witch is believed to live in them. When the mist came in you walked around for hours lost until you stumbled across a house where an old lady lives. When you are invited into the house and you enter you realized you had found the witch. When she placed her hat on her head she disappeared leaving the hat behind and with no way to return home you did the same. You now have to escape the cellar and find your way home.

Witch Hunt is a text only adventure with each screen describing your location as you type in your commands.

Published as part of "The Lockerby Collection" / a.k.a. "The Witch".

176015.overview:
Word Flyer is an educational word-matching game for children.

Made for 1 - 2 player head to head play, two birds stand atop a tower of letters on both sides of the screen. Single letters or up to 4-letter words appear on the screen, progressively enlarging and floating towards the player. The goal is to use the joystick to choose the correct word from the tower of letters, and quickly move the text to line it up with the floating words. The player must move quickly, as words will disappear from the screen. The games starts with simple 1-letter matching, but as the player matches words, a grey bar on the bottom of the screen will begin to fill. When the bar fills, the game progresses to a more difficult stage, with a total of 5 stages in total.

176154.overview: A wall street investment strategy game released as part of "Entertainer II - Brain Games" game pack. Wall Street is a 1 - 4 player stock trading game for the Commodore 64. Players take turns buying and selling shares to try to maximize their profits. They can also invest in real estate and money markets. Game time is divided into individual quarters.

176569.overview:
A text adventure game published as a type-in game in the book "Castles & Kingdoms".

FROM SONG OF THE RINGSNARED SAILOR (FREEROVER THE BARD ) 

The pilgrim entered the waterfront tavern with some trepidation. He'd never seen a Nautical before, only heard about them in the way most youths absorb the history of the Kingdom. The waterfront was dangerous in its own right, populated as it was with a mixture of Humans, Graylocks and Not men. Only the Nauticals were a pure species and they alone held the power of the sea. The pilgrim shuddered a little as he made his way to the bar. The casual observer who did not know about Nauticals would have been horror-stricken. The pilgrim's face was gaunt and stretched, ears pointed and blackening at the tips. The beginnings of lupine whiskers were forming on his cheeks, his teeth and nails had already lengthened. The pilgrim was becoming a werewolf. Surrounded by Nauticals, the pilgrim/werewolf nervously sipped his drink. Amid the chattering, growling and occasional howling of the Nauticals around him, his thoughts drifted back three months, to the polymorph's silver ring and a magic - all too rare in these enlightened times - which had transforming powers. Then reality crept in again and the pilgrim quaffed his drink. He ordered another. Captain Red watched the pilgrim at the bar with interest. He was not dressed like the ragtags he'd seen ringsnared in the past. This pilgrim was obviously a noble or the son of a noble. Captain Red was intrigued. Here was money to be made. The erstwhile Captain was well known amongst the Nauticals as a rogue. But he was also known for his temper ashore. The pilgrim had also heard of Captain Red. Lt was for that reason he'd chosen this particular tavern. He'd been told that Red, above all other Nautical officers, was the most competent seafarer there was, a rumor that he meant to test. "I be Captain Red." growled a voice at the bar. "Be ye lookin' for me?" 105 It has been said that the extrasensory perception of a ringsnared being are multiplied tenfold. It has also been said that Captain Red had, in his pre-lupine existence, been a telepath of great talent. The meeting that followed was both inevitable and productive. Midnight found the pilgrim at the harbor dockside, as arranged in the tavern.

176902.overview: A snake-style action game. Players guide a snake around a field with varying obstacles; the goal is to eat all of the mushrooms to proceed to the next level. Each time the snake eats a mushroom, it gets longer; a life is lost if the snake crashes into walls or itself. Published in Keypunch software's Adventure Quest IV game collection, as a game of "The Big 100" collection / a.k.a. "Worms" and in Your Computer magazine 1984/07.

177862.overview:
War in the South Pacific is an advanced strategic simulation of the land, sea, and air campaigns in the South Pacific from May 1942 to March 1943 between Japan and the United States.

Players choose from 79 different ship types and 17 different aircraft types. The game comes with 3 mini campaigns. Upon the conclusion of the game the computer will display the total points for each side and the net points scored. The net points will determine the level of victory. The game can be played solitaire or against another person and there are 5 levels of difficulty. Playing time is 25 to 100 hours.

178446.overview: Published in Computronic 1986/05-06, Pixel No.37 (10/1987), Digital Marketing PD #221 / a.k.a. "The Wheel" which is reminiscent of BC's Quest for Tires, but the object is as simple as a stone, just keep on rolling down the line and jump any obstacles to keep the wheels turning.

181752.overview:
Surf but avoid vortexes, mighty Neptune, surfmines, surfcatchers and the Titanic and get the high score. May the surfvirus be with you! 
 
Published in Italy as Windsurf or Wind Surf in Play on tape Nuova serie - Giochi d’Estate.

181945.overview: A Swedish take on Breakout/Arkanoid games. Very colorful.

181950.overview:
1988, the year War Cars Construction Set was released on Commodore 64, as well as ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC. Made by Software Creations Ltd. and published by Firebird Software, this racing / driving game was a racing\collect em up and was published in Italy as WarCars 3 in  Alga Soft 1988 n.12a.

The C64 version was never officially released, the Italian version was a pirated version.

182136.overview:
A horizontally scrolling space shooter in which a spacecraft is piloted similarly to aircraft controls. You will need to continuously dodge the enemy bases and overcome the areas equipped with electrodes from which high voltage potentials generated by nuclear power plants are discharged. Other bases are equipped with areas where hammers crush, and can damage your ship beyond repair. During the flight you will be attacked by other spaceships that arrive in formations and can change their attitude making an escape route problematic. Of course you can do more than dodge, activate your weapons to take down enemies before they careen into you. 

Published in Italy as Warfire in the Play on tape Nuova serie - Guerre Spaziali 6 collection and in Formula 64 n.89.

182137.overview: An updated version of Wildfire for 1991! The sequel to the horizontally scrolling space shooter, Delta clone.

182140.overview:
A single frame shooter where the vultures come at you from the sky and you must use your trusty shotgun to dispatch them. But careful, they are wily, you need to hit them in the wing to take them out. (Or possibly the collisions in this game are just really, badly programmed, so we'll make it a feature.)

Published in Amico Bit #2

182142.overview: A Halloween themed adventure game released for the Halloween Game Dev Competition 2019. Use a 1351 mouse in port 1 or a joystick in port 2, and try to figure out how this game controls. What is implemented is most of a puzzle it stops when the final ingredient is acquired.

182144.overview: 17 levels that were never commercially released. The last level is a joke and wasn't intended to be completed. You can cast levitate or feather fall while dying to save yourself. Comes with a level editor to make your own Wizard games.

182157.overview: A remake of the original game that came out in 1998 with 33 new levels to explore!

182208.overview:
The primordial cave-crawling strategy hunting game type is visited once again, with most of the fundamentals the same: the player is searching through a randomized maze for a stinky monster, the Wumpus, which can be neutralized from an adjacent room but will end the player's game if encountered directly.

 This version is from the book "101 Programming Surprises & Tricks for Your Commodore 64 Computer"

182209.overview:
An updated German version of the famous Hunt the Wumpus strategy and logic game. The core of the game remains identical with the player hunting a Wumpus in a cave system. It has the following additional random events: Earthquakes, bat migrations, and what is described as the "turnareo" which changes the layout of the cave.
 
Published in the book "More BASIC Computer Games - German Edition"

This version varies from the Wumpus I and Wumpus 2 games released in the English versions of this book.

182210.overview:
An updated version of Hunt the Wumpus. Gameplay is the same as the original; however, several new cave options are available.

The goal of the game is to shoot a mythical creature known as the wumpus with an arrow. The player explores a cave containing 20 rooms, several bottomless pits, bats, and the wumpus. The game will provide clues which the player needs to use to figure out the layout of the cave. For example, if the game indicates there is a breeze then one (or more) of the adjacent rooms contains a pit, or if there is a wumpus smell then the wumpus is nearby. On each turn the player can either move to another room or shoot an arrow; entering a room which contains either a pit or the wumpus ends the game. Occasionally bats are encountered, which may carry the player off to another room randomly.

Published in the book "Adventures for Your Commodore 64".

184267.overview: You've been left in charge of Bridgeton Asylum while the manager is away and you have messed up big time. You forgot to lock the main door and all the patients have gone out into the big bright world. You need to find them and round them all up before the manager returns and you get fired. Trouble at Bridgeton is a text adventure where text describes your location and any items of interest. You type in commands to control your player with the keyboard.

184366.overview: Wizard Fight is a 2 player only game in which one player controls a blue wizard, while the other controls a red wizard. The object is simple, destroy the opposing wizard before he destroys you. Published in Game On 1989/04.

185077.overview:
A scrolling shooter published in 64'er 1994/02. Jump'n'run and graphics freaks will laugh: this game is characterized not only by insane speed, but also by parallax scrolling over ten different levels! The "Walker" can be moved forwards or backwards, he can jump and activate his laser cannon by firing it. If you press the joystick to the right, the action takes off: The Walker races across the screen! On the way he encounters boulders.
Insects and giant banana leaves. 

You have to learn to shoot down these obstacles without thinking twice (or at least dodge them) - every touch, no matter how small, costs the walker 1000 points of his valuable energy supply (coupled with the score display at the top left). sinks you.  If the number is below 0, the message "Game over" appears and the number of points/energy achieved up to that point.

Parallax scrolling begins as soon as the walker crosses the center of the screen. If you want to change this position, you must enter before you start:
POKE 2924.32 ♦ X • 8; PCatE 6102.32: RUN X must not be greater than "13" (only integer numbers are permitted, i.e. without decimal places. 0 = left, 13 « right). For whom the game speed is too high. he can dim them a little with the slow-motion switch on the corresponding joystick!

185080.overview:
A breakout variant for you and 3 of your friends, published in Magic Disk 64 1990/05.

As the name suggests, The Wall has something to do with a wall. It is also correct that there is a ball in play, with which the said wall must be destroyed in order to reach the next level. As soon as the ball leaves the lower edge of the screen, it is lost and a ball from the storage chamber, which contains 9 balls, is made available. When all balls are used up, the game is over. But if you fend off the ball skilfully with the bat, it will take a while before it comes to that.

185114.overview: An English language fantasy themed text adventure written by Mike Doran in 1988. You are the assistant of Menra the Magician. Dran the evil wizard has stolen Menras wand and his gold. The magician is powerless without his magic wand and the people of Ghopasia are very angry that their cherished treasure is gone. It is now your task to return the wand and the gold to central-square of Ghopasia. But be careful, the wizards evil companions are ready to destroy you on your mission.

185116.overview: The player controls a scuba diver who moves continuously from the left of the screen, and can fire directly forwards. Enemy scuba divers move about the screen and fire back. The player can shoot the enemies for points, but they don't disappear from the screen. It's game over when the player is hit 3 times.

185117.overview: Strategy war game vs martian invaders based on the board game by Allen D. Eldridge.

185118.overview: One to four wizards may play. Prepare for the Quest!

185120.overview: A challenging SEUCK shooter published in ECP's "War Games Pak".

185121.overview: A SEUCK based shooter for one or two simultaneous and cooperative play.

185122.overview: A breakout/Arkanoid type game with some speech synthesis that you normally don't on a game sold this inexpensively. Published in Game On 1990/08.

185124.overview:
A horizontally scrolling space shoot'em up published in Commodore Zone Issue #04 (March/April 1996).

It was later released into the public domain by Binary Zone PD.

185125.overview: Pretty good shooter that isn't too tough to beat.

185127.overview: It's thermonuclear war! Break the computer code to launch your missiles, then guide your interceptors before enemy missiles converge with your cities. This is a game in two parts. The first part plays a lot like a sliding block puzzle. You are given a figure in a 3 x 3 grid to match. Using the joystick and fire button, you rotate pieces in a larger grid to try to match the smaller figure. If you do that, you can select a missile launch site. Eventually, the enemy will launch its own missiles. You position your crosshair at the radar dot for the enemy missile, and can then launch an intercepter. This part of the game is more action-oriented as you "fly" your intercepter to take down the enemy nuke

185130.overview: The battle for The Ancient Continent, a domination strategy board game. There are "shareware" and Registered full versions of this game.

185138.overview: A single-screen shoot'em up in the style of Muckle published in Commodore Zone Issue #16.

185139.overview: A Muckle-style single screen shooter, and sequel to the original Warpzone from 2001.

185142.overview: A cross between Hawkeye and Shadow of the Beast, Warrior is a sharp looking platformer that could compete (and win) against many C64 fully-priced games of the same era. Worth the play, it has a delightfully humorous ending. Also published in Golden Disk 64 1994/02.

185143.overview:
This is the sequel to the first part of the Warriors of Ras series, Dunzhin. All games in this series are early graphical Roguelikes. The story is quite simple: Enter the mystical monster-infested dungeon Kaiv, slay monsters and grab treasures.

You explore the dungeon in a turn-based manner by entering commands in text adventure, like "MOVE NORTH" or "LIGHT TORCH". The commands may be abbreviated by one or two letters. You can also move several squares at once (like "MOVE EAST 3") to speed up your quest. Another very helpful command is "SPEED", which makes the game's messages go by faster. Your progress is hindered by traps (acid pools, slimey floors etc., some of which you can escape by quickly pressing a key), thieves who rob you, random teleports and, of course, by a variety of 24 different monsters, ranging from simple Zombies, Wolves or Dwarves up to Wyverns and Vampires.

The combat system makes the Warriors of Ras series stand out from other roguelikes: Apart from your total hit points, you and the monsters also have hit points and armor for each body party separately. If the hit points of one body part reach zero, you're dead. Each attack must be directed to one of the body parts, some of which are easier to hit than others. You may also "AIM" a hit (which costs some time, but makes the attack more likely to hit) or "FORCE" an attack (this makes it more difficult to hit, but increases the damage). This and the body parts result in a quite tactical combat -- you have to guess or find out the weak parts of your opponent and choose the right way of attacking.

185272.overview:
The Wylde is the third part of the Warriors of Ras series of RPGs for multiple systems.

As told during the previous game Kaiv, Grimsweord the Warrior has returned from his adventure in the Kaiv ragged and lame. It is the hope of Lord Doserror that he might recover with the Wizard's magical help, but this has not come to pass. The only thing that might cure him is a healing item located deep within the Wylde. A young apprentice sorceress named Cwenellen has been chosen to seek out the healing unguent, and has been awarded 2000 pieces of gold and a map of the area to aid in this task.

Played largely from a fixed overhead map, the player starts in the castle in the southwest of the map, and attempts to recover a healing item located to the northeast. All commands including movement are via text commands. The town contains a store to purchase supplies, as well as allows the player to store gold. The player can only revisit the main town 5 times, or they are turned into a wild animal by the livid Wizard. The player can collect bounties on randomly chosen enemies for 100 gold if they return after slaying the creature. In the countryside, the player must contend with environmental damage, and the constant threat of hunger. There are 2 outposts, which allow the player to restock resources. The player must sleep every evening, and can get attacked in their sleep.

Combat occurs on a separate map, where the player encounters multiple opponents. The player and enemies takes turns moving and attacking, and the player has a total of 13 different locations they can attack on enemies and 9 separate body locations to defend, but if vitals locations are lost, the player perishes. The player can aim their attacks, or flail randomly. They can also choose more forceful attacks. The player can gain valuable items and weapons after combat, and will progressively level up and become stronger with successful combats. Magical items can be found in combat to give the player an edge.

Ultimately, the goal is to reach the location in the northeast, and defeat the guardian creatures. The player must then return to the town in the southwest to claim victory.

185278.overview:
Ziggurat is a first-person shooter similar to Tower of Guns that borrows many elements from the roguelike games. Game elements include permadeath, randomized environments and enemies, random pick-ups, weapons, items and skills. The game has a fantasy theme and the protagonist is an apprentice of the Greyborn citadel, established by the Daedalon brothers wizards, where aspiring wizards are trained. Their final test is the Ziggurat where novices go to die or survive and become part of the citadel's inner circle.

The tower-like Ziggurat consists of several floors that need to be completed with a single life. The game has permadeath but it is possible to save progress after completing a floor to continue another time. The game emphasizes fast-paced movement including sprinting, jumping and using platforms in the environment, fighting against large hordes in small rooms, but optionally auto-aiming can be enabled. Each floor is generated with a random pattern and it consists of several floors linked together by corridors. To complete a level a guardian boss needs to be defeated, but it can only be summoned when a portal key has first been located elsewhere. A typical room spawns a large amount of minions that need to be defeated before the doors open again. There is a chance of a random effect when entering a room, for instance creating larger enemies, doing more damage, making them invisible etc.

Other types of rooms that can be part of a floor are a treasure room with a powerful item, a hazard room where an environmental hazard needs to be avoided, a shrine where health or mana can be offered to the gods in exchange for an additional effect or modifier, and a lore room where an ancient scroll can be found, providing knowledge. Each floor also has a secret room hidden behind a cracked wall. Inside one of two skills can be chosen and it also shows information about one of the developer's earlier games.

At the start the player chooses one of several characters with different statistics and modifiers, presented as different classes, but only one is available in the beginning as the others are unlocked gradually. The default weapons is a magic wand that shoots projectiles. It has unlimited ammo, but requires some time for ammo to be refilled entirely. Three additional types of weapons can be picked up, tied to three limited mana sources. Each mana source offers several weapons per type, but only one per type can be carried at all times, so a maximum of four weapons in total. At the start of a floor a new weapon is always offered to optionally pick up or exchange. Each weapon has a regular attack, and a powerful attack that consumes more. Weapons include staffs, grenades, homing projectiles, charges that freeze opponents etc. They all use ranged attacks so the character needs to keep a distance, but still needs to move in to collect the items left behind by defeated enemies before they vanish.

185290.overview: A typing tutor game. The Warrior Words re attacking! To keep them from landing in your city, you must act quickly, to destroy a word, type it and push the space bar. You will score points for each word you destroy and get a bonus by destroying a blinking word. Watch out fo blitz attacks! This game has 6 levels of difficulty. Spelling game where user can set level and speed for grade 4 and above.

185294.overview:
The inhabitants of the Delta planet, Zypar are a truly unique people and have a degree of civilization that is unmatched throughout the galaxy. Their laws require that at the age of 18 they must challenge their peers in a special gym to decide their future. The challenge takes place riding an inertial platform with which you have to undermine the opponent or direct him towards the door of death where the photonic rays will disintegrate. Once you have destroyed your opponent you will need to collect his remains to be able to increase your score. You can defend yourself from photonics by taking the energy blocks present in the central hole of the gym. The final winner will be allowed to join the legion of rulers while the loser will have to choose between exile or slavery to the rulers. 

Published in Italy as Gli Sfidanti di Delta (Delta Challengers) in Super Game 2000 n.11 (Gennaio 1986) and Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - super top 30 (1987).

185298.overview: Try to complete all 15 levels. Collect falling gems and avoid the falling boulders and bricks. You can take a boulder hit and live but bricks will take you right out. Published in GO64! 2003/12, and also in GO64! 2003/05.

185302.overview: Published in 64'er Software Extra Nr.20: Spiele. Waterman or Aquarius a single screen platformer.

185317.overview: A feel very much like an updated version of Air & Sea Battle from the 2600. Take out the endless convoy of ships and avoid the depth charges fired from the plane. They will get you if they even get close to you.

185319.overview: Alfredo the Idiot returns to collect water avoiding the falling objects and making his way to the water bucket before the time runs out. Make your way to the container to fill it. You must pass back and forth several times to fill it up. The only game I know to have the "Morning Has Broken" as the theme. Published in the Italian, Soft 1984, #05 compilation release.

185329.overview: In Nepal there is a mountain called Annapurna. ON its summit there are many lakes, but in its depths are a complex of caverns in cold rock. The peoples living in Rajistan Valley need the water, so Micro must quickly dig galleries to make the water fall down. Set detonators for exploding the rock to make waterfalls so the water falls to the accumulator. There is a time limit so work quickly. Published in Italvideo compilation release.

185385.overview: An educational geography game using weather as the gateway to US geography knowledge.

185386.overview: In this artillery game, an enhanced clone of Ouranos!, feuding sides settle their disputes with aggressive weather patterns. On opposite sides of the screen, two players with some pull over local weather conditions take turns assaulting each others' castles with their pick of hail, rain, lightning or tornadoes. These attacks emanate from an itinerant cloud drifting variously across the top of the screen, and must be directed by a numerical "charge" value intended to account for a shifting wind speed and the location of the cloud. The winner is whichever party completely obliterates their opponent's abode first.

185387.overview: Weaver is an action puzzle/logic game developed by Peter Kaul in 1990 and published by Mark & Technik in 64'er Sonderheft 54

185388.overview: Weaver II is an action puzzler/logic game developed by Peter Kaul and published by Markt & Teechnik in 64'er Sonderheft 61, and also in 64'er 1999/08. It is the sequel to 1990's Weaver.

185390.overview: You have to uncover the secret development of the Mad Scientists Association (MSA). Satellites have detected a MSA Laboratory on the moon, codenamed Wega. You are teleported to the moon but must find your own way back to Earth. The game was developed by Ralf Werner and published under his own label (Ralf Werner Software) in 1983.

185393.overview: Welcome to the end of your sanity! WeirdWorld is an interactive fiction novel that puts you in control of the story by leting you become the main character in an evolving tale that will unfold as you make decisions and interact with the various elements in the world the story resides in.

185507.overview: Compete in crosshairs shooting contests. Published in Golden Disk 64 1991/01.  The five bone-hard disciplines of this great action game challenge even the bravest computer freak. Whether it's shooting a bottle, catching a calf or acting as a sheriff, excitement and action are guaranteed!

185509.overview: A competitive only game for two players created by Chris Willard and released either in December 1989 like the title screen says or in 1991 by Street Games.

185518.overview: An unofficial  version of the Wheel of Fortune created by D.J.B. Shibley and published by Panther Software.

185520.overview: A version of the Wheel of Fortune game developed by Vermes and published by Marex.

185662.overview: Prevent enemy helicopters from flying out of view on either side. Enemy helicopters can be shot with the continuous fire machine gun or when necessary with one of the 5 nuclear missiles. If the enemy reaches the side, you lose. Released as part of "Sky Fighters" game pack.

185663.overview:
Whirlybird is an arcade style game which puts you in control a military helicopter. Each level has two goals. Firstly, you must destroy an enemy naval vessel by traveling to an island to load your copter with a bomb, and then dropping it on the battleship. While you are thus engaged, you are beset by two fast moving motor-boats armed with diagonally firing guns whose bullets you must dodge. Once the ship has been destroyed, the next stage starts with black planes that rapidly moving from the left to the right of the screen. You must shoot down three of these planes and capture the crew after they bail out of the plane into the water. After three have been captured, you have a limited amount of time to return the prisoners to the island. If this time runs out, it is game over, regardless of how many of your five starting helicopters remain.

Each level is pretty much the same, except that odd levels are in daylight while even levels are at night time. The only way this affects game-play is that the black planes are only possible to spot at night if they pass in front of a white cloud. Later levels are made more difficult by the addition of a grey fighter plane which attacks you with increasing levels of ferocity as you are trying to destroy the black plane.
 
Published in Italy in the Nova Games n.13 (Ottobre 1987)  compilation pack.

185664.overview: A platformer set in the trapped and treacherous areas around and under the White House. Earn points by staying alive and picking up treasure.

185678.overview: You are a member of the S.A.S. and you have been sent to an American Embassy to shoot terrorists that are holding hostages. The game is a 1st person shooter with the whole embassy building on the screen. There are a number of windows and terrorists or hostages will slide past the various windows in a different colour top. As the people appear in the windows you are told what colour the terrorists are wearing and these have to be shot by moving a cross-hair and pressing fire. You have only six shots and when these run out then you must move to a cross-hair in the bottom left and shoot it to reload your gun. For every terrorist shot you receive a merit and collect enough before the time runs out and you are promoted. Shoot a hostage though then you are demoted and if you are demoted from Private or let the time run out then it is game over. During the game the colour of the terrorists can also change to a different colour.

185692.overview: You are Jack Stalk a detective and must crack your latest case.

185762.overview:
A Detective strategy text adventure game. Find the hidden necklace and solve the case. 
 
You are a down on his luck detective, who just got called to investigate a robbery at the Carr estate. The lights went out during a party to show off the new necklace, and when they came back on, the necklace was gone. The player must explore the Carr estate, and look for clues as to who stole the necklace and where it was hidden. The player can talk to the party guests, and explore the different rooms of the estate. After determining the culprit, the player must return to the paddywagon and say "case closed". All commands are via VERB NOUN entry. There is a save/restore feature available.

185778.overview: The year is 2025. Thanks to hard work and dedication, Burger King® has created a Whopper® that you don't need to go get, it will come to you. Of course, others want a Whopper® and some ingredients want to be extra on a Whopper®. But there is a hungry patron waiting so you must soldier on. In this game, you are the Whopper®. You must make your way to the right past all obstacles to get to the hungry patron. Along the way, you must also gather the parts to the Burger King® logo, so the patron knows you're a real Whopper® and not a knockoff. You must kill or avoid tomatoes and pickles that want to be on you and dogs, slingshot kids and kitchen brutes that want to eat you. You can shoot shots of ketchup at these beings but beware as the slingshot kid and kitchen brute can shoot/throw knives. The game was given away to people that ordered a Whopper® meal at Burger King® in 1987 in Spain as a promotion.

185780.overview: Part of "Fun in Learning" game pack. in this game by Thomas W. Wahlberg you can learn about the presidents of the US up until the time of release (Ronald Regan), where they were born and their birth and death years and be quizzed on that information.

185793.overview: Bonus demo game on original disk of "Quedex". In this game, Willy returns to have a go at inertial movement.

186187.overview: Window on a Maze is a customizable labyrinth/maze game developed by S.T. Burke and published in Your Commodore 1989/08.

186393.overview: Window-Cleaner is a simple platform game coded in BASIC. It was developed by Greg Hopkins and published as a type-in game in the book "PCW Games Collection for the Commodore 64" in 1984.

186404.overview:
Winged Lizard is a shoot 'em game for 1 or 2 players (simultaneously) in which you play the character(s) of a flying lizard/dragon taking on enemies such as skeletons, demons, witches, etc.

It was developed by Mike Futcher using Chris Yates' SUECK engine in 1993.

186626.overview:
Filbur Apse was a particularly obnoxious person, who enjoyed upsetting and annoying anyone and everyone he came into contact with. One day, however, he went too far, annoying a seemingly harmless old man who turned out to be a wizard in disguise. As a punishment the wizard cast a spell which changed Filbur so that he was no longer obnoxious - and took all the fun out of his life! Can he find the magic ingredients that will make him thoroughly detestable once more?

Part of the Classic Quests series.

186627.overview:
An electronic version of the Mastermind type board game published in 64 Tape Computing No. 10 (1985/08).

Has a whopping maximum players of 999.

186865.overview: 1984's Wizard, created by Sean Moore and Steve Luedders and published by Ariolasoft and PP&S included a level creator\editor which spawned other creative people to create additional levels and challenges. This is one o those, a modification of 33 New Levels (Custom) and includes Wizard Game Construction.

186867.overview: A new set of expert levels for Wizard, made with Wizard Game Construction.

186868.overview: Sequel to Wizard Expert I, this is an additional set of expert levels created with Wizard Game Construction.

186871.overview: Spook needs to escape from the King of Id's dungeons. He slips out but Turnkey is in pursuit. He needs to solve math problems to open the way to his escape. Wizard of Id's WizMath is an educational game to teach mathematics. Using your joystick, you must move blocks into place so they complete a correct math problem and answer. If you push against a block, you will send it flying until it hits a wall or another block. You can also face a block and hold down the button. While keeping the button down, you can then slide the block as needed. There is a sixty second time limit and you are being pursued by Turnkey. Early levels require only one math problem to exit but later levels require two or more. Early in the game, you can select a floor on an elevator. The higher the floor, the more difficult the math problems. The game also asks your age. The older you say you are, the higher a floor it tries to start you on, although you can select a lower floor.

186876.overview:
An educational Grammar and spelling game with 6 subgames:
Jester's Jumble, 
Dragon's Spell,  
Word Spinning, 
Herald's Hark, 
and King Author.

186880.overview: A PETSCII graphics 2D RPG game similar to Quest but with Dungeons and Dragons to add a little flavor. The original add promised two to five hour playing time and the "world" was randomly generated at the beginning of each game, so every game instance was just a little different.

186882.overview: A Gauntlet style shooter published in 64'er Software Extra Nr.21: Spiele.

186884.overview: A single player scrolling-screen platformer created by Pim van Vriezen and Published by CP Verlag.

186885.overview: Wobbler is an action game created by Cyberstyle and published in both Game On 1990/08, and Game On GE 1991/2.

186888.overview: Navigate the dangerous labyrinth, just don't touch those walls or obstacles!

186898.overview: Nerkus the Wizard has kidnapped Sherlie, and transformed her beloved Dave into an iron ball. As Dave, you must set off to rescue her from Nerkus’ castle, by completing the zones that guard a magic door. Wonderball is a scrolling action game in which you control the constantly bouncing Dave, guiding him over water hazards and spikes, and away from contact with the many meanies he will encounter, such as Fireflies and Gugglies. Navigating a path through the chaos often requires pixel-perfect placement, particularly as enemies come into play based on your position in the level, rather than based on time. You start with 5 Daves. Entering the yellow Underground sections lets you play a simple game of chance, in which lives can be gained or points gained or lost.

186903.overview: A simple text adventure coupled with PETSCII graphics. Developed by Mark D. Rejhon and released into the public domain in 1986.

186910.overview:
A Worm/Snake game that allowed for 3 and 4 players through use of special cable and a second computer. Developed by Image Design and published by CP Verlag.

Note: in order to play 3 and 4 players, you need a special cable and 2 computers connected.

186913.overview: The Woodpecker must keep the Sacred Tree alive. Use the holes to capture your prey and help keep the tree healthy and well.

186916.overview: Poor Pepito the sheep is lost in Mindspace! You must help him escape from this nightmare by guiding him through 16 levels guarded by Green Martians, Space Chickens and Wiggly Worms! WOOLLY JUMPER is the full 64K version of the game Richard originally wrote for the RGCD 16K Cartridge Compo. It now features enhanced graphics by WEC and improved jump physics.

186917.overview: An educational game focused on Grammar/Spelling.

186918.overview: Word Challenge is a 1-player word forming game similar to the Parker Brother's game Boggle. In standard mode, players are given a 4 x 4 grid of 16 randomized letters, with the goal of making as many 3-or-more letter words as possible in a period of time. Words must be formed by using the next nearby letter, and each letter can only be used once in forming a word. The game includes a built-in dictionary, and only available words may be used to score points. The player competes against a computer opponent, with the goal of typing more correct words in a given time period than the computer opponent discovers. Players can modify the skill of the computer opponent, timer time, size of the game board, scoring method, and other aspects.

186941.overview:
These educational games with the Mr. Men characters from Roger Hargreaves' children books are for kids aged 5 to 8 years. It features these fun games that also develop reading skills:
Mr Noisy's Word Game: Learn about opposites, comparatives and superlatives. There are nine different games to play, each of which can be selected from the main menu. Other games allow various combinations of reading and writing exercises ranging from matching up a picture with the correct word to choosing the opposite to a displayed word.
Read with Mr Bounce: Learn words like 'above', 'inside', and 'on'. Again, there are several different options to teach different uses of the words.
Included with the game is a specially designed keyboard overlay with clear 'small' letters cutting out the confusing clutter on a computer keyboard and an illustrated instruction book to help an adult introduce the program to children, plus separate notes on the programs and the educational aspects. 
 
Contains "Mr. Noisy's Word Game" and "Read with Mr. Bounce".

186943.overview: Printer required, solve the word search and the game will quiz you on your answers. Single player game created by  J. Lewis, Len Lindsay and released by Cue in 1983.

186944.overview:
Test you word knowledge! Age guide 11+ Content: 1200+ words in five sections: synonyms, similes, collectives, nouns and their adjectives.
The purpose of Wordpower is to expand vocabulary and improve spelling. Most people suffer from a restricted code-they use the same words and sentences again and again because they don't know how to say or write the same thing in different ways. Wordpower enriches your use of language by showing you alternatives and making you use words accurately. Start with one of the two games- 'Lines' is easier than 'Shooting, "and then when you are sure you know the words, get the spelling right with the writing option.

186945.overview: A platformer where you make your way through a a shifting level picking up diamonds and items that will help you modify the level to allow you to clear it in the time you have given. 3 difficulty settings allow you to skip ahead to the harder levels.

186946.overview:
A 1-player boxing game published in Commodore Zone Issue #16.

The game is keyboard only.

186947.overview:
An ice hockey game where you can play for either the world cup or choose a practice match. World cup play can include up to 9 players. On the ice there are two teams that face each other and put the puck into the goal. The winner is whoever has managed to do this the most at the end of  90 seconds plus a possible overtime. You control one player at a time and you can recognize him by his jersey color. The computer will try to allow you control of the player closest to the puck.  
 
The Italian version named Hockey Pista changed the game description have the game be roller hockey and refers to the puck as a ball. It was published in International Games n.7 (luglio/agosto 1991).

186948.overview: This football simulation focuses on international football, allowing you to play a tournament or single friendly matches. Up to 8 human players can be involved in the tournament. Options include three skill levels, variable match lengths and a choice of sound or music (or both on some versions). The match is viewed from the side, although it switches to a 3D view when the ball is close to the goal. The ball roughly sticks to the player's foot. Set pieces are controlled by moving an aiming cross-hair.

186951.overview: World Class Casino Blackjack is a blackjack/21 card game developed by C.J. Tantini and published by Nova Computer Software in 1984.

186991.overview:
World Cup Football is a football game allowing you to play in the World Cup. The game allows you and eight other friends to choose a various amount of teams to get to the final and win it. The computer plays as the remaining teams not selected. The game itself is viewed from the side above the pitch and the screen shows part of the pitch and scrolls when you move your player. A joystick is used to control your team with the fire button used to pass and shoot. Throw-ins, goal-kicks and corners are included.

The C64 version is slightly more limited than the Spectrum version, as the Spectrum version has 40 selectable teams, whereas the C64 version only has 16.

187058.overview:
If you initially suspect small, cute doodle monsters behind this cute name, you will be taught better after the first few seconds of play. "Wozzle" is a pure thinking game that does not use other programs as a model. "Wozzle" is independent, brilliant and is characterized by an addiction factor that should not be underestimated. At the start of the game a playing field appears, the left half of which is randomly shuffled. The object of the game is now to restore this field to its original state, which is shown on the right-hand side.
The individual stones can be rotated by clicking with the joystick, whereby all adjoining stones also rotate. But only if the stones really touch each other, i.e. if there is a connection between them.

Published in Magic Disk 64 1993/07.

187065.overview: Part of "Survival Instinct" game pack. This racing game has 4 levels of difficulty chosen using the function keys. Your car starts on the right side of the screen and you must avoid other vehicles heading towards you as well as the pit crews that are trying to block you in. Stay out of the pits and go as long as possible.

194400.overview: Wix-Wax is a simple side scrolling shooter. It was developed by Jewels and Published in Italy's Alga Soft 1988 n.3b in 1988.

194459.overview: Wizard's Doom is a Sokoban inspired puzzle game that takes part in a castle. This game was developed by Richard Hansen and published in Loadstar #076.

194461.overview: Ling awakes in Baron Baranov's dungeon. The baron fears all creatures of the night and Ling knows that her dark heritage is the reason for her imprisonment. Can she escape from the dungeon? Can she break her curse?

194610.overview:
This is a top secret mission.

In the year of 2035, scientists at the HADRONICS research facility managed to successfully create a WORMHOLE.

It connected the Earth to an alien planet far away in the universe. However, shortly afterwards, hostile aliens invaded the laboratory and kidnapped the Professor, who is the only person capable of stopping the experiment. A rescue mission was started and YOU were chosen to save the world.

Equipped with a rocket-driven Hazmat suit, you have to make your way through the research facilities, go through the WORMHOLE and rescue the Professor.

WORMHOLE is a side-scrolling jump 'n shoot game for the legendary Commodore 64.

It contains 15 challenging, diversified levels, divided into three different chapters. The game can be played as one- or two player game (alternating, only one active player at a time) using one or two joysticks, optionally. Three different weapon systems (pistol, lasergun and rocket launcher) are available in the game that help to eliminate various types of alien creatures on your way through the dangerous environment of the research facilities and the alien planet.

In addition, you can collect bombs that can be detonated either via remote control or by time fuze. Also make sure to collect additional fuel for your horizontal and vertical rocket drive. The built-in trainer helps you to familiarize with the different levels, and to prepare yourself for the next attempt on a new highscore!

196916.overview: A worm\snake game published in Ahoy! 1985/05 (Issue #17) as a type-in tutorial on how to handle the logistics of manipulating colors separately from characters in your original game programs, using snake as an example.

196920.overview:
Worm! is rather original take on the snake variant in which you must eat all the mushrooms and then find the exit to get to the next level while avoiding or shooting the Grim Reapers roaming around the maze. In order to shoot you must first collect bullets that can be found around the maze. 

As in all Snake variants, every time you eat a mushroom your body gets longer, making it increasingly difficult to avoid Mr Reaper.

Published in Italy as Serpentone in Special Program n.84 (febbraio 1992) and in Hit Parade C64 n.67 (Maggio 1992).

197286.overview: Published on a type-in book "Micro Wars on the Commodore 64" that featured six strategy games,  Waterloo is a multiplayer game that deals with the Battle of Waterloo in which Napoleon Bonaparte was defeated by two of the armies of the Seventh Coalition. Can you change the course of history?

199312.overview: Exciting poker that offers you double-folds as soon as you are in the process of winning money. Written by Thierry Ducrocq and published by Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

199416.overview: When the people began to drain the swamp, the swamp spirits made their escape to a unknown world  with the only available magic vacuum cleaner, but a swamp spirit has swallowed up the departure and must be dealt with. Also published in Power-Games (Bestell-Nr. 38785).

200715.overview: A four player wrestling game created by Kevin Burk and published by KAB Software. Now 1-4 players can enjoy all the thrills of the Wrestling action you have been watching on TV, but now on your home computer! With the unique 2-4 player Tag Team Mode you can invite up to 3 of your best friends or 3 of your worst enemies to join you in the ring. If you have been slammed one too many times then make your way to the corner and tag your teammate's hand. Now you can rest while your partner tries to pin the opponent. Use Pro Moves like the Pile Driver and the Body Slam off the rope. Elbow drops, back breakers and drop kicks are all fair game. Choose from 13 different wrestlers including some of the craziest characters ever to enter a wrestling ring.

202036.overview: Wheels of Steel is a pretty decent albeit simplistic homebrewed horizontally scrolling motorcycle racing game for the Commodore 64. This game was developed by Alan Bond and released into the public domain in 1986.

202066.overview:
In the original versions of Wheel of Fortune created by I.J.E Inc, some versions in conjunction with Softie Inc had a major flaw, bad randomization of questions and an error where some sets of questions would never be used. 

BYB, of Hokuto Force, fixed the randomizer and allowed the game to present every possible puzzle in addition to improving the fastloader. After finishing a complete games round, puzzles used are saved together with the highscore to disk, meaning your next game and the following ones won't repeat for a very long time. 

A computer version of the popular game show Wheel Of Fortune, where you guess letters until you can guess the phrase. Three old-school rounds of Wheel of Fortune (where the puzzles are simply "Phrase", "Title", "Person", etc.) and then a bonus round. You can compete against 2 computer players or up to three people can play against each other.

202086.overview: A very basic translation of the popular game show Wheel Of Fortune, where you guess letters until you can guess the phrase. This version has three old-school rounds of Wheel of Fortune (where the puzzles are simply "Phrase", "Title", "Person", etc.) and then a bonus round. You can compete against 2 computer players or up to three people can play against each other.

202228.overview:
A Sabre Wulf style game with a hint of platform action thrown in for good measure. Bas-refief graphics were used to good effect to give the perception of depth going into the screen. For instance, you could only run over platforms when they were at the correct level. The game also included some jazzy parallax scrolling and all kinds of nice little features. Unfortunately, it would never be released by Firebird in the UK and was lost to time.  
 
Then in 2015 Games That Weren't helped recover a copy of it, but found the version they had wasn't quite finished in places. So Richard Paynter, the original author came back to decompile and fix it all, as well as including an intro, music, better sound effects and as of May 23, 2021 released it back to the scene with a final version on June 6th of the same year.

205447.overview:
Word Master is a 1-player educational game for multiple systems.

A word appears in the center of the screen, and 8 surrounding words slowly fire towards the player. The player must rotate a turret to shoot the antonym of the word that appears in the middle of the screen. If the player shoots the correct block, a new word appears in the middle of the screen. The player must shoot all 8 words before the approaching gunfire reaches the center of the game field.

205668.overview: A one to six player party game created by Luciano Merighi and Jörg Rosenstiel of Merifon and published in both Commodore 64 Club #06 [Italian Release], and in Commodore Computer Club Nr.3 [German Release]. A collection of work related mini games to blow off steam after a hard week.

206679.overview: A Worm\Snake game published in COMPUTE! 1984/04 (Issue #47) and in the Street Games "Red Box" release in Australia and New Zealand. The game is featuring Nerm the Worm, who is trapped in Bemer Castle and would like nothing more than to escape (and consume a generous helping of "magic mushrooms" along the way). Yet another variation on Snake where the player controls a serpentine crawler in perpetual motion, which must be guided to consume food, dodge deadly walls, and avoid biting its own tail. The castle is composed of eleven rooms, each trickier to navigate than the last. In a vaguely Carrollian manner, the rooms are prone to sprouting mushrooms which cause Nerm to grow as he eats them: after consuming five mushrooms, the exit doors will open, leading to the next room. Extra lives are awarded along the way, presumably another effect of the magical fungi.

207776.overview:
Wardots is a grid based board game for the Commodore 64. It is single player, but can be played with up to three computer opponents, you can also choose the "aggression" level of each opponent.

Developed by Kate and Ron Slaminko and published in Loadstar #196.

208582.overview:
The Boulder Dash Club Freudenberg was a club that was founded to swap Boulderdash games between Boulderdash fans. In that time Internet was not as important as it nowadays is, so a club like this one was pleasant for the Boulderdash players who had created own games or who wanted to play others' creations.

Rolf Roth, the father of Marek Roth (who are both well-known people among the Boulderdash fans) sent all his games to the Boulder Dash Club Freudenberg. Once he won an award for the best title screens in his Boulderdash games and he got a lighter.
 
This version translates to Waterfront and and there were a total of 8 games known in this series.

208631.overview: Worldcup-Skiing II is a homebrewed downhill skiing game for the Commodore 64. It can be played with up to 9 players alternating turns. The game was developed by M. Müller, A. Knoblauch & R. Bölstler (of Knobbe Soft) and released into the public domain in 1987.

208861.overview:
The preview was originally released for Halloween 2020, with updates released for each spooky season since. This good looking platformer was created by Carl-Henrik Skårstedt and the Space Moguls crew. 
 
A young witch has moved in to town and opened her missing persons rescue agency. Interesting cases await in this platforming escapade!

208864.overview:
A puzzler that is reminiscent of Lemmings but with stones and a robot you need to guide carefully to the end. There are also trick blocks that will allow the robot to fall and must be discovered through play and lifts that will elevate the robot to the top of the section it is in and teleporters.

Published in 64'er 1993/08.

209200.overview: White Water is a single player water sports/racing game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Tim Hanson and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1989/11 (Issue #77).

209206.overview: Ferry skiers across the gap on 3 levels. You can only lose so many and your days of skyway transport will be cut short. Published in Software Club N°19 and as Cabs in Commodore Club - software # 19 and in Hit Parade C64 n.37 (Settembre 1989).

210246.overview:
Wizard's Demons by Troy Heck puts you in the role of a wizard's apprentice, whose master has just been cursed by a sinister rival wizard. While your master hobbles around his courtyard in a mindless trance, demonic minions of the rival scream overhead, waiting for a chance to snatch your master and send him on a one-way trip to their summoner's lair.  
 
You, the lowly apprentice, with a few tricks from your studies, are all that stand between your master and his tortuous death. 
 
The game was initially released as part of COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1994/06. At this point it was a disk only publication. It was re-released with updates by Army of Darkness in 2021.

210579.overview:
A Shoot'em Up Construction Kit based action game, released in 1996 with an enhanced version released on 19 June 2007. Poor Snodge the Biblet... just when we thought things were bad, the worst is yet to come for our poor herd. He has been captured and thrown into the deepest depths of the water. It is up to you to help poor Snodge try and reach the banks of the 4 challenging stages. All is not easy though, as there are deadly creatures that live in the deep water. Luckily for Snodge, he can make bubbles that can kill those deadly creatures. Watch out, as they can fight back! If you are careful enough, you will succeed!

This was an updated version of Snodge's Water Caper from 1995.

211630.overview:
After robbing the bank, your rough, tough and ready desperado colleagues have fled into the scrubland, dropping their guns and the loot. Well we all know that a man, or a Calamity Jane, has got to do what ever it is. So, you are on your own outside the bank and you have to make it to the horses, which some idiot left on the outskirts of town. On the way you can collect money and guns with bullets and then decide, if you run into the Sheriff's posse, whether to bribe or blast your way to freedom. Obviously your aim is to reach the horses with some bullets and some money. We are not advocating here that crime pays — that is up to you.  
 
Use the ARROW keys to make your moves. Your footsteps will appear on the screen as you move toward the horse in the top left hand corner of the screen. Your progress will be recorded on the bottom of the screen, and you will, in your progress, be told that you have run into the posse, and you will then be asked if you intend to shoot or bribe your way out. Key in SHOOT or BRIBE Should you run out of bullets I'm afraid that a lynching is
your fate, as the posse were playing poker when you robbed the bank, and the Sheriff had a Royal Flush. If you reach your horse, you will hear the galloping as you ride off into the sunset.  
 
Western Adventure Game was created by Geneviève Ludinski and published in the book "Brainteasers for the Commodore 64" in 1983.

213356.overview:
"Who Wants to Waste an Afternoon?" is a quiz game for the C64. It was heavily inspired by "Who Wants to be a Millionaire?". It was developed by Lee Novak and published in the following...

Loadstar #195 +#196 + #197 + #198 + #199 + #201 + #202 + #203 + #208 + #211

213707.overview: Compose and play a musical score using an easy graphical interface and toolkit. Use a pointer to drag notes, sharps, and other music nomenclature directly onto a staff, then play your creation. You can cut, copy, and paste entire sections of music, as well as print your masterpiece.

214147.overview:
Webster's Numbers is an an educational math game for 1 or 2 players in a team. The game was developed by EduWare Services under their Dragonware series label and published by Britannica Software, Inc. in 1985.

The game had an official certification by the National Education Association (NEA).

215576.overview:
In a remote corner of the galaxy, the planet Obid is is suddenly assailed by a meteor storm. As this ancient planet hurtles through the rocks, its greatest city, called Im, is threatened with annihilation. A city council is hastily assembled and a decision unanimously struck: Send for the Wizard of Im

You are the Wizard of Im. Brandishing a magic wand that hurls huge fireballs, you set forth to destroy the deadly cascade of rock and spare the city. Despite your powers, however, it remains to be seen if you are quick enough to blast the multitude of menacing meteors before they fall to earth,

The game is easy at first, but like a lot of shooters of this type, the falling meteors increase in speed as the game goes on.

The Wizard of Im was developed by Bob Spirko and published as a type-in game in Ahoy! 1985/07 (Issue #19).

217355.overview: Collect the apples while avoiding the wasps in this German language collect 'em up. An unofficial English translated version was released in 2015 by Hokuto Force.

217357.overview: A SEUCK based shooter created in 1989 by Jim Butterfield (Outlaw-Emix Software). Avoid touching your foe's boats, ships, subs and mines to make your way further and further into the hostile enemy base. Blast out the bridges that may be blocking your progress. Blast the turrets and avoid the helicopters. See how deeply you can penetrate their defenses.

217358.overview: A SEUCK based shooter by Outlaw-Emix Software published in 1991. Gun down the desperadoes that are out to bury you in Boot Hill. A game for one or two players and includes cooperative mode.

217359.overview: An 8 player game from Petr Chlud for party fun. A fun word game for the right 8 geeks. Search for words in a constantly changing array of letters using the joystick. if you don't have 8 PLAYER ADAPTERS, you can use joy in port 1 and 2. the menu allows you to choose the game adapter, change the name of the players (joy right), the length of the game, vowel highlighting, hiding words, the rate of letter change and complete change of the play field after word approval ...

217360.overview: A ROM hack by MML of the 1985 SSI game Kampfgruppe but instead of depicting a WWII battle in Germany it depicts the beginnings of WW3.

217590.overview: A horror story set in the derelict Westbury House. This text adventure, written by Dorothy Millard using the Quill\Adventurewriter system was released in 1993 by The Adventure Workshop.

218528.overview: Wilde 15 is a number based logical brain/puzzle game. It was developed by Jan Lindenberg and published by Europa Computer-Club in 1985.

218744.overview: Worm: The Final Battle (also known as The Worm) is a Snake/Worm game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by TDR! and released into the public domain in 1989.

218749.overview: Worm! is your typical snake/worm game. This version was developed by Graham " Toki" Axten and released into the public domain in 1996.

218808.overview: A game by Steven T. Chapman, author of Quo Vadis this is a game for those in search of the next step in 3D graphics adventures. Wizardry fwas a 3-dimensional graphic adventure, loosely in the style of "Dungeons & Dragons".  It implemented magic and melee combat against multiple enemies, and involved a lot of puzzle solving. The music was extremely good for the time, and the tune played was in line with what was happening in the game.

219666.overview: A single player SEUCK based game from Giuseppe Vollaro (Pinov Vox) with a holiday theme, released for the Halloween Game Dev Competition 2019. Something had gone bump in the night. Well, Halloween may be over, but there's one game which never got released yesterday, as it was to be first submitted to a Halloween C64 game development compo, run by DoubleSided games. This is a spooky, but fun arcade adventure, created with the Shoot Em Up Construction kit, called Wizmax. You play a magician's ball, which has to break a spell of an evil witch, which has raided the good magician's castle. She put the magician to sleep, and has sprayed power crystals in the rooms of the castle. Wizmax must eat those crystals, before getting caught by the evil ghosts, skeletons and other monsters. Then face the witch and destroy her to break the spell.

219727.overview: "We Are Stardust (The C64 WASD game)" is a game for the Commodore 64 included on the physical versions of the LukHash album with the same name: "We Are Stardust". This game has until  now only been available as a physical game, but is now available as a free digital game. This digital version is slightly modified and has a new loading tune composed by Lukhash. If you want to obtain the physical version, read below for more information. The game is an infinite runner created by Jamie Fuller and Megastyle in 2021.

220132.overview:
Will 0' the Wisp is a great adventure game for devious and nimble minded computophiles. Trudging through a vast forest in the guise of a fairly simple minded woodsman, and destined to wed the fair Brunhilde on the morn, the player seeks a final day of adventurous freedom before the dread shackles of marriage are fixed firmly about his ankles. The poor fool recklessly throws his life on the mere whims of the program until, eventually, more by good luck than management, he finds himself outside the Great Cave.

Tempted in by a floating wisp of mist the player ventures fearlessly on, then to his surprise a rumbling sounds behind him, the doors to the cave swing shut, and the only way to go is onwards. Dread horrors await the fearless woodland yokel, and this is all you are going to get, dear Reader. Onward and may the best yokel
win!

418967.overview: White Wash is a board game for up to two players (also has an AI vs AI demo mode) for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Peter Weighill and published as part of Commodore Disk User's Games Disk 4 in 1991.

421107.overview: A multi-game release for the C64 created using Assembler: A release which not only features a miniature Windows desktop, but the ability to play games from an early Windows OS such as Solitaire, Freecell and Minesweeper!
